subject: ENG
course_description: An inquiry into the various expressions of human desire through readings of selected works of literature. Topics may include romance, psychoanalysis, gay and lesbian studies, or the four loves, classically conceived.
course_notes: This course will explore sentiment and feelings through the lens of Black queer and women writers from Africa and the African Diaspora. This course will investigate themes of loss, longing, love, and desire as a mode for expressing racial, national, gender, and sexuality politics. We will compare the literary histories of African and African American literature to critique constructions of national literatures as well as canonization. We will determine how desire informs the construction of bodies of literature and investigate comparative themes across different spaces.¿ We will read poems, plays, novels, and watch films related to the course themes. ¿As critical learners, we will practice how to write about difficult topics keeping the complexities of humanity in mind. The course will cover these questions: How is desire a political concern? How is romantic love a metaphor for writing? How can we read text where queerness is obscured? What is the role of literature in responding to different political contexts? Some authors we will read in this course are Gayl Jones, Yvonne Vera, Alice Walker and Noviolet Bulawayo.
